column1: # The red run: this tree's assertions against the engine the base ref holds,
# written whole by tests/red, which tests/run --record-assertions calls.
#   base  <ref>  <sha>  <engine version there>
#   run   <failed>  <passed>  <skipped>        lines counted, not the summary
#   <assertion name>  <times it failed>        failed names only
# A base of - means no red run was possible. Reproduce with: tests/red <ref>
base
run
--dir pointed at one project's directory reads the transcripts in it
--dir with no value exits non-zero
--since counts the stops on or after the cutoff, read against what came before it: a check the day before is stale, not never
--since keeps the cut day, drops what came before it, and splits a session across it
--since refuses a month of 19 and a day of 39, where a real date runs
--verify adds to what counts as a check
--verify refuses a backslash class, which is a class on one awk and a letter on another, where [[:space:]] runs
a $( ) standing as the command, quoted, runs what it holds, and a path built on one is the program: 3 checks beside a built path that runs no tests
a --since that is not YYYY-MM-DD exits non-zero
a -c script whose here-document body runs past the first 64K goes on after the body to its closing quote, over 256K as under it: the runner there is a check
a 6 MB command holding 300,000 backslashes is read in seconds, with the default checks and with a --verify that holds a backslash: under 10 each
a << that opens no here-document, a shift or one in quotes, reads the same on either side of 256K: the runner after it is a check, and a sed -i after a check leaves the stop stale
a VAR=$( ) or a backquoted value before a runner is an assignment, so the runner is a check; assigning a path built from one is not
a VAR=value ends at ; or a line break, and assigning a gate's path is not running it: a copy or a quote after one is no check
a backslash at the end of a comment does not join the next line to it: the runner there is a check, and a --silent after a commented-out flag takes npm test's status

a cd inside a subshell, a $( ), a -c script or a shell's here-document ends with it: the relative write after it is an edit after the check, and one after a cd in a { } group or the command itself is scratch
a check is read from the command, not the description, and a parallel call's error does not fail the check beside it
a check that ends a { } or ( ) group whose output is redirected could have been seen to fail; only the one another command in the group follows is counted as could not
a command of 10,000 << shifts, none of them a here-document, is read in one pass: under 5 seconds
a command of 26,000 runners costs no more than twice the CPU of one of the same shape holding one: the last is found in one read
a directory or a dangling link named like a transcript, sorting last, is skipped and the run exits 0
a double-quoted -c script is read with its escapes taken off: a program path quoted inside it is the program, and text quoted inside it is text
a failing piped check is counted failed, and the report does not say a piped check's result is never marked an error
a leading --no-commission is the flag, while any other leading flag is still refused as a name
a line ending in one backslash goes on to the next: an && list across it can fail, and a path on the next line is an argument
a line of two tool_use blocks is read block by block, and an error is charged only to the result block that reported it
a megabyte line of backslashes, content blocks or timestamps is read in one pass: three sessions in under 15 seconds
a passing check whose exit status a pipe, a later command or the background took is counted as one that could not fail: 3 of 5
a person's message that starts with pasted stop hook feedback is not a hold; the hook's own meta record is
a quoted program path at command position is the program: "$W/.venv/bin/python" -m pytest and "$FELIX_HOME/harness/felix" gate are checks, "npm test" as a name is not
a runner after if, do, ! or { is a check, and 3 of the 4 hand their status to the if, the loop or the !
a runner at the start of a here-document line is text handed to a command, not a check
a runner in bash -c '...' or in a here-document fed to bash is counted as a check, or the report says such runs are not seen
a runner in markdown backticks inside a one-line commit message is not counted as a check
a runner inside one-line double-quoted text, a grep or pgrep pattern or an echo, is not a check; a runner whose own argument is quoted still is
a runner named in a here-document, a single-quoted pattern or a multi-line message is text, not a check; one after a quoted path is
a script handed to bash -c or sh -c over 256K is read at both ends: a runner at its start or its end is a check
a session filed under two projects, and history copied into a resumed one, count once: 2 sessions, 1 stop, 1 hold
a session is read without its subagent files, which would add a check, a stop and a hold
a shell comment is not code: its apostrophe opens no quote, its (npm test) runs nothing, and its ; takes no status
a sidechain edit does not turn a pass stale, and a failure reported before its tool_use_id, behind an escaped quote, still fails
a stop and a hold copied into a resumed session belong to the session their record names, whichever transcript sorts first: 2 stops and 2 holds in 2 sessions both ways
a stop is a distinct message id: a stop logged again is not a second one, and a failing non-check fails nothing
a tool_use with its type key first is read by its own id and name, not by an id or a name nested in its input ahead of them
a transcript that cannot be opened is named in the report, not silently left out
a transcript with no timestamped record is said to be skipped for it, counted and in the singular or plural, beside sessions or none
across every run, no file appeared, vanished or changed under the scratch root
after the last audit run as after the first: nothing changed under the scratch root outside the review fixtures, nothing in the scratch HOME, and no claude, gh, curl or wget was called
an edit to a scratch file or to Claude's own config directory is left out of the four, and the report says how many stops that was
an edit to a skill under Claude's configuration directory or to Felix's memory is left out as no gate's, and the report and the README name that scope
an empty directory is reported as no transcripts, exit 0
an escaped quote in a -c script is not its close where the cut after the first 64K falls inside the escape: the runner at the script's end is a check
an explicit --dir that is not a directory is refused, where the same run on a directory exits 0
an unknown flag exits non-zero where the same run without it exits 0
and calls no claude
and no claude, gh, curl or wget was called
and nothing in the scratch HOME changed: no .felix-home, no .felix, no .claude
and prints one line saying commissioning was skipped and felix commission runs it later
and reads them in under 30 seconds
and runs none of commissioning: no run, no receipt, no discovery cache, no commissioning log
and the passed class claims only that no error was reported
and with CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR unset, HOME/.claude/projects
failed is exactly 1: the last check after the last edit failed
felix audit --dir exits 0 over a directory of transcripts
felix audit --help answers its usage and reads nothing
felix audit runs with bash and awk alone on PATH, as the README says, and answers the same report
felix commission, run later, commissions what felix new --no-commission created
felix new --no-commission that could not write its marker binds the checkout when run again, once it is writable
felix new <name> --no-commission creates the project, binds the checkout, and seeds what a commissioned one gets
felix new refuses a third argument, a mistyped --no-commission or any other, before it makes anything or calls claude; spelled right, the same command binds
felix new refuses any flag but --no-commission, first, second, third or fourth, naming it as a flag beside the synopsis, before it makes anything or calls claude
felix new with a flag or a missing directory where the path goes is refused before anything is made
felix new's usage line names --no-commission
felix with no arguments lists felix audit in the grouped help
it counts 10 stops after edits, in 6 sessions
it counts 4 Felix holds in 3 sessions, not a quoted, sidechain, subagent or foreign stop hook
it counts every stop in 41,400 lines: 450 passed and 450 failed
it counts the seven top-level sessions it read, not the subagent files or the stray one beside them
it gives the date range from record timestamps, 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-09, not a date quoted in a message
it names the directory it read
it names what counts as a check and that --verify changes it
it says edits and checks inside subagents are not seen
its first line says it is read-only
its last line points at felix new <name> --no-commission
neither the help nor the audit says --no-commission governs with nothing installed; both name felix install
never is exactly 3: no check at any point in the session before the stop
no line of the report, of felix audit --help or of felix's help says a turn ended, since a held stop did not
of 3 held stops, the hold line counts among the stops above only the 1 that followed an edit, not the 2 after turns with no new edit
passed is exactly 4: the last check after the last edit did not fail

sed -i, perl -i, a > or >> to a named path, tee, patch and git apply are edits: after a passing check the stop is stale, alone it is a stop, to scratch it is left out; the report and the README say other writes through Bash are not seen
so is a machine where Claude Code never ran, exit 0
so the same command with the flag spelled right then binds it
stale is exactly 2: no check after the last edit, one earlier in the session
the README lists by path exactly what the audit leaves out: /tmp, TMPDIR, CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude, FELIX_MEMORY or ~/.felix/memory
the README names all felix audit runs, bash through /usr/bin/env, awk, and readlink where felix is reached through a symlink, which bash and awk alone cannot follow
the README's Try it section shows felix audit from a clone and felix new <name> --no-commission, and names felix install as what holds sessions
the audit runs above are wired to the read-only checks: an engine that writes under HOME and calls claude, run through the same wrapper, shows in that HOME and in the stub log
the default checks reach the runners of more ecosystems, and the flags and wrappers before them: 28 commands, each a check, beside 2 that run none
the flag between the name and the path binds the path given
the flag is what made the difference: the same felix new without it calls claude and writes a receipt
the grouped help names --no-commission

the help, the audit and the README say in the same words that a --no-commission project's sessions are held once felix install has run where a gate was guessed, and to set gate in project.json first where none was
the hold line claims no more than the hold does, and says a held stop is counted
the log a group's or a compound's own output goes to is not a write after the check in it: 6 such read passed, and a write after the group is still stale

the never line claims only what the roster recognises, and --verify ERE adds a project's own runner to it, in every project read, as the report, the help, the README and ecosystem.tsv say; none claims every ecosystem
the read-only checks can fail: an audit that writes under HOME and calls claude changes the snapshot and the stub log
the shares are whole percentages of the stops after edits
the word pipefail in an echo does not make a piped check able to fail: 1 of 2 passing checks could not have
three 5 MB commands dense in << or in line breaks are read in seconds, not minutes, and each still passes: under 30 for the three
whose record, when and whether a sidechain are read from the record's own keys, and a tool_use with its type key last is read
with neither HOME nor CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set it reports no transcripts and exits 0
with no --dir it reads CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects
